source: Karnataka NMMS SAT 2020-21 question paper, NMMS-SAT-P2 (K-8) (pyq/ka-2020-21-sat.pdf), English version. The paper has no answer key.

questions.subject: physics
questions.prompt: The distance-time graph for a uniform motion is :

options.D: Straight line making 45° with the x-axis.

solution.concept: 8.4 Uniform motion: equal distances in equal times
steps: Distance grows by the same amount every second, so the distance-time graph is a straight sloping line
A line parallel to the x-axis means the object is at rest; a curve means non-uniform motion; a line parallel to the y-axis is impossible
D is the only straight sloping line

questions.subject: physics
questions.prompt: The device which works on the principle of magnetic effect of electric current is :

solution.concept: 4.1 Electromagnets: a coil carrying a current acts as a magnet; electric bells use one
steps: An electric bell’s electromagnet pulls the hammer to strike the gong
A fuse, a bulb and a heating coil work by the heating effect of current

questions.subject: physics
questions.prompt: The image formed by a concave lens is :

solution.concept: 10.4 Concave lens: it always forms an erect, diminished image
steps: The image is always erect
It is formed on the same side as the object and cannot be caught on a screen: it is virtual

questions.subject: physics
questions.prompt:
With respect to land and sea, the correct statements are :
a) Land heats up faster
b) Sea heats up faster
c) Land cools down faster
d) Sea cools down faster

solution.concept: 7.2.1 Land and water: soil heats up faster than water and also cools down faster
steps: Land heats up faster (a) ✓
Land cools down faster (c) ✓; so b and d are false

questions.subject: physics
questions.prompt: If an object oscillates 20 times in 5 s, then its period is :

solution.concept: 8.1.1 Time period = total time ÷ number of oscillations

questions.subject: physics
questions.prompt: If the amplitude of a sound wave is increased 2 times, then its loudness increases by :

solution.concept: Old syllabus – Sound: loudness is proportional to the square of the amplitude
steps: Amplitude × 2 gives loudness × 2²
2² = 4 times

questions.subject: physics
questions.prompt: The audible frequency range of the human ear is :

solution.concept: Old syllabus – Sound: humans hear sounds from about 20 Hz to 20,000 Hz
steps: Below 20 Hz is infrasound and above 20,000 Hz is ultrasound
So the audible range is 20 Hz – 20,000 Hz

questions.subject: physics
questions.prompt: The force exerted by a charged body is :

solution.concept: 5.4.2 Electrostatic force: the force exerted by a charged body
steps: A charged body attracts or repels other bodies without touching them
That force is the electrostatic force

questions.subject: physics
questions.prompt: The advantage of using ball bearings in machines is :

options.A: Sliding friction changes into rolling friction.
options.B: Rolling friction changes into sliding friction.
options.C: Static friction changes into rolling friction.
options.D: Static friction changes into sliding friction.

solution.concept: 5.4.1 Friction: rolling is resisted much less than sliding
steps: Ball bearings let the parts roll over each other instead of sliding
So they change sliding friction into the smaller rolling friction

questions.subject: physics
questions.prompt: The pressure exerted by liquids does not depend on :

solution.concept: 6.1 Liquid pressure depends on the depth of the liquid, not on the width of the container
steps: Pressure at a point depends on the height of the liquid above it, the liquid’s density and gravity
It does not depend on the area of the liquid surface

questions.subject: physics
questions.prompt: Sound waves can travel through :

solution.concept: Old syllabus – Sound: sound travels through any medium: solids, liquids and gases
steps: We hear through air, whales call through water, and a sound on a table carries through the wood
Only a vacuum stops sound

questions.subject: physics
questions.prompt: The resultant of two forces acting on a body is zero if the forces are :

options.A: Unequal in magnitude and acting in the same direction.
options.B: Equal in magnitude and acting in the same direction.
options.C: Unequal in magnitude and acting in opposite directions.
options.D: Equal in magnitude and acting in opposite directions.

solution.concept: 5.1 & 5.2 Balanced forces: forces that cancel give a net force of zero
steps: Two forces cancel only if they are equal in size
and act in opposite directions

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.prompt: The man-made fibre obtained from a natural source is :

solution.concept: Old syllabus – Synthetic Fibres and Plastics: rayon (artificial silk) is made from wood pulp
steps: Rayon is man-made, but from cellulose obtained from wood pulp, a natural source
Nylon and polyester come from petrochemicals; cotton is a natural fibre

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.prompt: An example of a plastic which cannot be softened on heating is :

solution.concept: Old syllabus – Synthetic Fibres and Plastics: thermosetting plastics do not soften when heated
steps: Bakelite, once moulded, does not soften on heating (it is used for switches and pan handles)
Polythene and PVC soften on heating (thermoplastics); terylene is a fibre

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.prompt: A versatile material used in the manufacture of fire-resistant cloth is :

solution.concept: Old syllabus – Synthetic Fibres and Plastics: melamine resists fire and heat
steps: Melamine is a thermosetting plastic that does not catch fire easily
It is used in fire-resistant cloth (firemen’s uniforms) and kitchenware

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.prompt: The solution that conducts electricity is :

solution.concept: 4.3.1 Voltaic cell: the electrolyte is an acid or a salt solution, which conducts electricity
steps: Salt dissolved in water conducts electricity
Kerosene, petrol and a glucose solution do not

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.prompt: The conditions under which dead vegetation turned into petroleum and natural gas are :

options.A: absence of air, low temperature, high pressure.
options.B: presence of air, high temperature, low pressure.
options.C: absence of air, high temperature, high pressure.
options.D: presence of air, low temperature, high pressure.

solution.concept: Old syllabus – Coal and Petroleum: petroleum and natural gas formed from buried remains of sea organisms
steps: The remains were buried under layers of sand and clay, away from air
Over millions of years, high temperature and high pressure turned them into petroleum and natural gas

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.prompt: The process of separating the different components of petroleum based on their boiling points is :

solution.concept: Old syllabus – Coal and Petroleum: refining petroleum by fractional distillation
steps: The parts of petroleum boil at different temperatures
Separating them by their boiling points is fractional distillation (refining)

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.prompt: The ignition temperature of inflammable substances is :

solution.concept: 5.3.2 Ignition temperature: the lowest temperature at which a substance catches fire
steps: Inflammable substances (petrol, LPG, alcohol) catch fire very easily
So their ignition temperature is low

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.prompt: The correct matching of the constituents of petroleum and their uses :

options.A: a - iv, b - ii, c - iii, d - i
options.B: a - i, b - iii, c - ii, d - iv
options.C: a - iii, b - iv, c - i, d - ii
options.D: a - ii, b - iii, c - iv, d - i

solution.concept: Old syllabus – Coal and Petroleum: uses of the parts of petroleum
steps: Petrol – aviation fuel (iii); diesel – electric generators (iv)
Paraffin wax – ointments (i); bitumen – road surfacing (ii)

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.prompt: The unit of the calorific value of a fuel is :

solution.concept: Old syllabus – Combustion and Flame: calorific value is the heat given by burning 1 kg of a fuel completely
steps: Heat is measured in kilojoules and the fuel in kilograms
So the unit is kJ/kg

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.prompt: The suffocating and corrosive gas released by burning coal and diesel is :

solution.concept: Old syllabus – Combustion and Flame: coal and diesel contain sulphur, which burns to sulphur dioxide
steps: Sulphur dioxide (SO₂) is a choking (suffocating) gas
It dissolves in rain to form acid, which corrodes buildings and metals

questions.subject: biology
questions.prompt: The correct statement about fertilisers :

options.C: Provides a lot of humus to the soil
options.D: Relatively less rich in plant nutrients

solution.concept: Old syllabus – Crop Production and Management: fertilisers are man-made inorganic salts; manure is organic
steps: Fertilisers are made in factories and are rich in particular plant nutrients (N, P, K)
Manure is organic, gives the soil humus and is less rich in nutrients, so A, C and D describe manure

questions.subject: biology
questions.prompt: The microorganism that reproduces only inside the cells of the host organism :

solution.concept: 2.3 Viruses reproduce only inside the cells of a host
steps: Outside a host cell a virus cannot multiply
Bacteria, fungi and protozoa can reproduce on their own

questions.subject: biology
questions.prompt: The correct matching of scientists and their contributions :
table: ii. Discovered the vaccine for smallpox

options.A: a - iv, b - i, c - ii, d - iii
options.B: a - iv, b - ii, c - iii, d - i
options.C: a - iii, b - ii, c - iv, d - i
options.D: a - i, b - iii, c - ii, d - iv

solution.concept: 3.5 Vaccines and antibiotics: Jenner made the smallpox vaccine and Fleming discovered penicillin
steps: Fleming – penicillin (b – i); Jenner – smallpox vaccine (c – ii)
Pasteur studied fermentation (a – iv) and Koch found the anthrax bacterium, Bacillus anthracis (d – iii)

questions.subject: biology
questions.prompt: The process of loosening and turning the soil :

solution.concept: Old syllabus – Crop Production and Management: preparing the soil: tilling (ploughing)
steps: Loosening and turning the soil is tilling or ploughing
Sowing, harvesting and threshing come later

questions.subject: biology
questions.prompt: Farmers used to grow legumes as fodder in one season and wheat in the next season. By this method the nutrient replenished in the soil is :

solution.concept: 2.4.2 Rhizobium in the root nodules of legumes fixes nitrogen
steps: Legumes carry Rhizobium, which turns nitrogen from the air into compounds plants can use
Growing legumes between other crops (crop rotation) puts nitrogen back into the soil

questions.subject: biology
questions.prompt: The source book that keeps a record of all the endangered animals and plants :

solution.concept: 12.7–12.9 Conservation: endangered species are listed so that they can be protected
steps: The Red Data Book records all endangered plants and animals
There is no blue, yellow or green data book for this

questions.subject: biology
questions.prompt: The correct sequence of the life cycle of the silkworm :

solution.concept: Old syllabus – Fibre to Fabric (Wool and Silk): the silk moth’s life cycle
steps: The moth lays eggs, which hatch into larvae (silkworms)
A larva spins a cocoon and becomes a pupa, which develops into an adult moth

questions.subject: biology
questions.prompt: The parts of the pistil among the following :

solution.concept: 13.5.2 Parts of a flower: the pistil is the stigma, the style and the ovary
steps: Pistil (female part): stigma, style and ovary (with ovules)
Filament, anther and pollen belong to the stamen (male part)

questions.subject: biology
questions.prompt: The machine called ‘combine’ is a combination of :

solution.concept: Old syllabus – Crop Production and Management: harvesting and threshing machines
steps: A combine cuts the crop (harvester) and separates the grain (thresher) in one machine

questions.subject: biology
questions.prompt: The reproductive part of the Bryophyllum plant :

solution.concept: 13.5.1 Vegetative propagation: Bryophyllum grows new plants from buds on its leaf edges
steps: Bryophyllum’s leaves carry buds along their margins
A leaf on moist soil grows new plants, so the leaf is the reproductive part

questions.subject: biology
questions.prompt: The process by which a tadpole develops into an adult frog :

solution.concept: 13.5.2 Frogs: the zygote grows outside the body into a tadpole, which becomes a frog
steps: The big change in body form from tadpole to adult frog is called metamorphosis
Budding (Hydra) and regeneration (Planaria) are asexual; fertilisation comes before the tadpole

questions.subject: biology
questions.prompt: In the given diagram of the female reproductive system of a human, the parts labelled a, b and c respectively are :

solution.concept: 13.5.2 Sexual reproduction in animals: the female makes eggs (ova)
steps: a: the oval body beside the tube is the ovary, where eggs form
b: the tube with the fringed end that carries the egg is the oviduct
c: the large central chamber is the uterus

questions.subject: maths
questions.prompt: The number of lines of symmetry that a regular polygon of ‘n’ sides has is :

solution.concept: Lines of symmetry of regular polygons
steps: An equilateral triangle (3 sides) has 3 lines of symmetry, a square (4 sides) has 4, a regular hexagon has 6
A regular polygon of n sides has n lines of symmetry

questions.subject: maths
questions.prompt: On simplifying (aᵖ/aᵐ)ⁿ × (aᵐ/aⁿ)ᵖ × (aⁿ/aᵖ)ᵐ we get :

solution.concept: 2.2 & 2.3 Laws of exponents: aᵖ ÷ aᵐ = aᵖ⁻ᵐ, (aˣ)ʸ = aˣʸ and a⁰ = 1
steps: (aᵖ/aᵐ)ⁿ = a^(np − nm), (aᵐ/aⁿ)ᵖ = a^(pm − pn), (aⁿ/aᵖ)ᵐ = a^(mn − mp)
Add the exponents: np − nm + pm − pn + mn − mp = 0
The product is a⁰ = 1

solution.concept: 8.2 Division of fractions: dividing by a fraction is multiplying by its reciprocal
steps: The reciprocal of 6/7 is 7/6

questions.subject: maths
questions.prompt: The side of a square park is 100 m. A path 5 m wide runs all around the park on the inside. The cost of cementing this path at the rate of ₹250 per 10 m² is :

solution.concept: 14.1 Rectangular paths: path area = outer area − inner area
steps: Inside the path the square is 100 − 2 × 5 = 90 m wide

questions.subject: maths
questions.prompt: In a regular polygon of 8 sides, the measures of each exterior angle and each interior angle are respectively :

solution.concept: Angles of a regular polygon: the exterior angles add up to 360°, and interior + exterior = 180°
steps: Each exterior angle = 360° ÷ 8 = 45°
Each interior angle = 180° − 45° = 135°

questions.subject: maths
questions.prompt: The difference between the least composite number and the least prime number is :

solution.concept: 3.1 Prime factorisation: primes have exactly two factors, composite numbers have more
steps: Least prime number = 2
Least composite number = 4 (factors 1, 2, 4)

questions.subject: maths
questions.prompt: Which one of these statements is always true?

options.A: All four interior angles of a rhombus are equal
options.B: All four sides of a kite are equal
options.C: All four sides of a rhombus are equal
options.D: All four interior angles of a kite are equal

solution.concept: 4.4 Rhombus: a quadrilateral with all four sides equal
steps: A rhombus has all four sides equal by definition
Its angles need not all be equal, and a kite has only adjacent pairs of equal sides and one pair of equal angles

steps: So it is always divisible by 99

questions.subject: maths
questions.prompt: The sum of a(b − c), b(c − a) and c(a − b) is :

solution.concept: 6.1 Distributive property: a(b − c) = ab − ac
steps: ab − ac + bc − ab + ca − bc
Every term cancels with its opposite
Sum = 0

questions.subject: maths

questions.subject: maths
questions.prompt: The perimeter of a rectangle whose length and breadth are (x + 1) cm and (x − 1) cm respectively is 24 cm. The length of the rectangle is :

solution.concept: 7.1 Framing an equation: perimeter of a rectangle = 2 × (length + breadth)
steps: Length = x + 1 = 7 cm

questions.subject: maths
questions.prompt: If an angle is half of its complement, then the measure of the angle is :

solution.concept: 5.2 Perpendicular lines: two angles that add up to 90° are complementary
steps: Let the angle be x; its complement is 90° − x

questions.subject: maths
questions.prompt: In a polygon, if the number of triangles obtained by drawing all the possible diagonals from one vertex is 18, then the number of sides of the polygon is :

solution.concept: Polygons: the diagonals from one vertex cut an n-sided polygon into n − 2 triangles

questions.subject: maths
questions.prompt: If the three-digit number 3y1 is exactly divisible by 9, then the value of ‘y’ is :

solution.concept: 5.2 Divisibility by 9: the sum of the digits must be divisible by 9
steps: 4 + y = 9, so y = 5 (the next multiple, 18, would need y = 14)

questions.subject: maths
questions.prompt:
Statement (i) : Rational numbers are not closed under multiplication.
Statement (ii) : Integers are closed under division.

solution.concept: Closure: a set is closed under an operation if the result always stays in the set
steps: (i) The product of two rational numbers is always rational, so rational numbers ARE closed under multiplication: (i) is false
(ii) 1 ÷ 2 = 1/2 is not an integer, so integers are not closed under division: (ii) is false

questions.subject: maths
questions.prompt:
Observe the figure. Among these, the true statements are :
i) b + f = c + e
ii) f + b + d = 180°
iii) a + b = d + e

solution.concept: 5.1 Intersecting lines: vertically opposite angles are equal, and angles on a straight line add up to 180°
steps: Vertically opposite pairs: c = f, d = a, e = b
(i) b + f = e + c ✓
(ii) c, d and e lie on one side of the vertical line, so c + d + e = 180°; f + b + d = c + e + d = 180° ✓
(iii) a + b = d + e ✓

questions.subject: maths
questions.prompt: The students of Class VIII in a school together donated ₹10201 to a flood relief fund. If each student gave as many rupees as the number of students in the class, then the number of students in the class is :

solution.concept: 1.1 Square roots: if n × n = N then n = √N
steps: Number of students × number of students = 10201
There are 101 students

questions.subject: maths
questions.prompt: Which one of the following numbers is exactly divisible by 3, 6 and 9?

solution.concept: 5.1 & 5.2 Divisibility: divisible by 9 and by 2 means divisible by 18 (and so by 3, 6 and 9)
steps: 162: digit sum 9 (divisible by 9) and even ✓
168: digit sum 15, not divisible by 9
172: digit sum 10; 179: digit sum 17, and both fail
